comment: MiniDAQ's problem reports (Chapter 14). tools/anomalies.py checks every report and generates known-anomalies.md from the open ones. Dates are when the book found the problem.

reports.title: A number outside the range of double crashed the configuration reader
reports.description: json::out_of_range (406) escaped the reader, which caught only json::parse_error; '6e688' ended the process.

evaluation.rationale: A crash during configure is a lost scan if it happens at the scanner; no wrong value was ever accepted.

reports.title: A sequence jump of 2^31 was counted as two billion lost packets
reports.description: Serial-number arithmetic is undefined for a distance of exactly 2^31; the tracker took the jump as a gap.

evaluation.rationale: Loss counters are how an operator judges a scan's completeness; a false count of two billion lost packets hides the real loss.

resolution.change: A jump beyond the maximum gap is a restart of the numbering (a resynchronization), not a loss.

reports.title: A new run could not open its UDP port while the previous run's detector held it
reports.description: The service created the new run's ports before it released the previous run's, so a second run failed with 'address in use'.

evaluation.rationale: The second scan of a session could not start: a delay, and a repeated injection if the tracer decays meanwhile.

resolution.change: The service releases the previous run's pipeline and ports before it creates new ones.

reports.title: take_all_goods counted a pair twice with per-single windows
reports.description: With a window per single, the pair (a, b) was formed from a's window and again from b's.

evaluation.rationale: Duplicated prompts bias the counts and the image quantitatively without any visible sign.

resolution.change: Only (opener, later single) pairs are resolved in each window.
resolution.verification: CoincidenceSorter tests for SRS-SRT-002, SRS-SRT-003 and SRS-SRT-009

reports.title: SOUP: nlohmann/json 3.11.3 may parse an integer as a float when errno holds EINTR
reports.description: Fixed upstream in 3.12.0 (#4506). The control server parses requests after poll(), which can return EINTR.

evaluation.rationale: The configuration reader requires integers, so such a value is rejected with a config_error and the operator sends the request again; no wrong setting is accepted. A request id may be echoed as a float.

reports.decision: Release with it; upgrade to 3.12.0 as a planned SOUP change (Chapter 16).

reports.title: A port fault is noticed up to 20 ms late
reports.description: The service's monitor polls the ports every 20 ms, so a run continues for up to 20 ms after a detector or sink fault.

evaluation.rationale: Data acquired in those 20 ms after a fault is part of a run that ends in a fault anyway; the fault is reported and the run is not used. No data is presented as complete.

reports.decision: Release with it; Chapter 15 decides whether a hazard needs a faster reaction.

reports.title: The sorter holds its last 104 ns of singles until more data arrives
reports.description: A single can only be judged when a later single shows that its window is closed. A source that falls silent leaves up to the window plus the delay of singles in the sorter until the end of the run.

evaluation.rationale: The singles are processed at the end of the run, so no coincidence is lost; only their latency grows while the source is silent.

reports.decision: Release with it; time markers from the readout would flush the sorter (Chapter 23).

reports.title: The control API has no authentication or encryption
reports.description: Any local process that can connect to 127.0.0.1:7700 can configure, start and stop acquisitions.

evaluation.rationale: A local attacker or a misdirected script can stop a scan or change its settings; the audit trail records it but does not prevent it.

reports.decision: Do not release for use beyond a test bench before Chapter 17's controls are in place.

reports.title: Simulation code is linked into the shipped server
reports.description: The synthetic source and the detector simulator are part of minidaq_core, so minidaq_server contains them and a configuration can select them.

evaluation.rationale: A clinical acquisition configured with a simulated source would produce plausible but invented data. The run record states the source type and metadata carries 'simulated', so the data is identifiable.

reports.decision: Release with it for 0.3.0 (MiniDAQ is a teaching project); a product build excludes the simulator or refuses it outside service mode.
